thread:
alex_cust: Hi team — we rotated our IdP signing cert at 09:12 UTC and since then SSO stops at the final redirect. Users see a 403 and our logs show "SAMLRecipientCheck failed: recipient mismatch". No other changes on our side. Anyone seen this after a cert rotation?
ava_support: Sorry you hit this, Alex. Can you paste the exact error from the SP logs and confirm the IdP metadata URL you updated? Also do you have a proxy/broker in front of the SP?
alex_cust: SP log snippet: "ERROR SAML: Recipient mismatch. expected=https://app.customer.example.com/sso/acs got=https://proxy.internal/broker/xyz". IdP metadata URL is https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata.xml — we updated cert there. Yes we have an internal broker/proxy that terminates at proxy.internal and forwards to the app.
lee_eng: That log is the smoking gun — the AssertionConsumerService Location in the SP metadata doesn't match what the IdP saw. If the proxy rewrites Host/Location or terminates TLS and sends a different Host header, the IdP might have recorded the ACS that includes the proxy host. Did the proxy change during the cert rotation?
miguel_oncall: Quick checklist: 1) confirm metadata.xml on the IdP shows the SP ACS URL you expect 2) confirm the cert fingerprint actually rotated and the IdP serves the new cert 3) check if proxy sets X-Forwarded-Host / Host override.
saml-bot: Metadata fetch: sha256 fingerprint for idp.customer.example.com cert = 3A:5B:...:EF (served at 09:15 UTC). Metadata content includes <AssertionConsumerService Location="https://proxy.internal/broker/xyz" index="0"/>.
alex_cust: Wait — when we uploaded the new cert we also flipped a staging flag on the proxy config. That caused host rewriting to include the internal broker path in the SP entity metadata that the IdP pulled. We didn't realize metadata fetch would pick that up.
ava_support: Ok that lines up. Two remediation options: (A) revert the proxy host rewrite (recommended) so the ACS Location remains https://app.customer.example.com/sso/acs and then force an IdP metadata refresh; or (B) update your SP configuration so the SP accepts the broker's ACS as a known recipient (less ideal).
lee_eng: For debugging, you can reproduce locally: curl -v https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata.xml | xmllint --xpath 'string(//md:AssertionConsumerService/@Location)' - 
You can also run the SP verifier against the raw SAMLResponse to see what Recipient is asserted: echo '<SAMLResponse...>' | base64 -d | xmllint --format - | grep Recipient -n.
miguel_oncall: If you prefer, we can trigger a metadata refresh from our side once you revert the proxy change — send the exact metadata URL and we'll force a pull and send a fresh validation report.
alex_cust: I rolled back the proxy staging flag and re-uploaded the original SP metadata to the IdP. Can you pull and confirm? URL: https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata.xml
saml-bot: Pull result at 09:58 UTC: metadata now contains <AssertionConsumerService Location="https://app.customer.example.com/sso/acs" index="0"/> and includes the new cert fingerprint. No chunked/gzip issues.
ava_support: Can you try signing in now (incognito) and paste the SAMLResponse error if it still fails?
alex_cust: Trying now... Login succeeded for me. A few test users confirmed access restored. Thank you.
lee_eng: Follow-up recommendation: prevent automatic metadata regeneration from the broker during maintenance windows, and add a quick validation check in your deploy pipeline that fetches IdP metadata and verifies ACS Location equals your canonical app host. Snippet example: 
```
curl -s https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata.xml | xmllint --xpath "//md:AssertionConsumerService/@Location" - | grep -q "app.customer.example.com" || echo "ACS mismatch"
```
ava_support: Glad that's fixed — marking this resolved for now. If you want, we can run a post-mortem to add a check to the staging proxy to avoid overwriting SP metadata. :thumbsup:
